s01.text: Before a model can read your sentence, something has to chop it into pieces.

s02.text: Those pieces are tokens, and they come from a tokenizer.

s03.text: The tokenizer is trained on a specific corpus, so it learns what is common in that corpus.

s04.text: Common things become one token. Rare things get chopped into several.

s05.text: English text is well represented, because most tokenizer training data is English.

s06.text: Other languages are not. The same meaning costs more tokens.

s07.text: And that is not a rounding detail. Tokens are what you are billed for.

s08.text: Same answer, more tokens, higher price.

s09.text: You can see it directly. Take one sentence and translate it.

s10.text: English takes a certain number of tokens. Another language takes more. A different script takes far more.

s11.text: Which is a tax on every language that was not in the training corpus.

s12.text: There are fixes. Train the tokenizer on more languages, or drop the tokenizer altogether.

s13.text: Until someone does, the token count is not a measurement of the text. It is a measurement of the tokenizer.
